scope: GSE292469 transfer of fixed Maynard17 alveolar score; depth, ambient RNA and gene-program interpretation
conclusion: No new biological mechanism or new general method established. A reproducible cohort-specific measurement audit may be useful if tests demonstrate an unresolved effect beyond known artifacts.

evidence_tiers.primary_methods: Establishes prior art; not direct evidence of the mechanism in GSE292469
evidence_tiers.patient_observational: Association in sampled tumors; not causal treatment effect
evidence_tiers.preclinical_intervention: Perturbation evidence in stated models; not clinical efficacy
evidence_tiers.primary_analysis_code: What code implements; does not prove every deposited output was reproduced
evidence_tiers.simulation: Conditional consequences of explicit assumptions; not patient validation
evidence_tiers.hypothesis: Proposed falsifiable explanation, not a finding

source_ledger.title: Normalization of single-cell RNA-seq counts by log(x + 1) or log(1 + x)
source_ledger.finding: Log-pseudocount expectation and conditioning on positive counts can distort comparisons. This already excludes novelty of the generic log1p/zero-selection artifact.

source_ledger.title: Normalization, redux: downsampling instead of scaling
source_ledger.finding: Explicitly demonstrates residual library-size effects after log normalization and downsampling as a sensitivity analysis; notes information loss.

source_ledger.title: Feature selection and dimension reduction for single-cell RNA-Seq based on a multinomial model
source_ledger.finding: Multinomial UMI sampling null and normalization-induced false variation are established; such a null is not a new model.

source_ledger.title: MAST: a flexible statistical framework for assessing transcriptional changes and characterizing heterogeneity in single-cell RNA sequencing data
source_ledger.finding: Detection versus positive abundance, cellular detection-rate covariates and residual coexpression analyses are established ideas.

source_ledger.title: Signature-scoring methods developed for bulk samples are not adequate for cancer single-cell RNA sequencing data
source_ledger.finding: Cancer signature benchmarking already uses within-cell downsampling followed by renormalization as a technical null and compares rank-based and expression-based scores. It does not validate the present 17-gene score.

source_ledger.title: UCell: Robust and scalable single-cell gene signature scoring
source_ledger.finding: Within-cell ranks reduce dependence on dataset composition. Composition robustness is not a guarantee of depth invariance.

source_ledger.title: Some important parameters for UCell
source_ledger.finding: The authors advise choosing maxRank with regard to detected-gene counts, explicitly acknowledging sparsity sensitivity.

source_ledger.title: SoupX removes ambient RNA contamination from droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing data
source_ledger.finding: Ambient mixture correction and negative marker/cell controls are established; no-expression assumptions must be defensible.

source_ledger.title: Single-Nucleus RNA-Sequencing Profiling of Mouse Lung. Reduced Dissociation Bias and Improved Rare Cell-Type Detection Compared with Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
source_ledger.finding: Healthy mouse lung nuclei show ambient epithelial contamination; SoupX improves many markers but Sftpc is incompletely removed. This is direct lung prior art, not proof of contamination in these human tumors.

source_ledger.title: Therapy-Induced Evolution of Human Lung Cancer Revealed by Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
source_ledger.inspection: Project signature source verification and primary paper
source_ledger.finding: The 17-gene alveolar signature and residual-state observation are published prior art. Reusing it is external application, not signature discovery.

source_ledger.title: Complementary modes of resistance to EGFR TKI in lung adenocarcinoma through MAPK activation and cellular plasticity
source_ledger.finding: Original 62-patient preprint reports declining patient-aggregated alveolar/LUAD/MAPK signatures and heterogeneous persister states. It uses UCell and malignant metaprograms, not a demonstrated identical Maynard17 score.

source_ledger.title: egfr_nucseq author code
source_ledger.inspection: 15 key files retrieved; relevant sections inspected
source_ledger.finding: Current code uses SoupX-corrected UCell scoring, sample/library integration, specimen-average comparisons, QC plots, and a depth-adjusted gene-level mixed model. Different stages have different adjustments.

source_ledger.title: Malignant alveolar metaprogram referenced in trajectory code
source_ledger.finding: This trajectory-input set overlaps 9 of 17 Maynard genes. It is not proof of the exact contents of the separate current 67-metaprogram score CSV.

source_ledger.title: Epigenomic analysis identifies DTP subpopulation using HOPX to develop targeted therapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma
source_ledger.finding: HOPX-associated persister heterogeneity, transient lineage-gene induction and delayed regrowth after HOPX deletion are already reported in treated models; this is not a new target proposal.

source_ledger.title: ASCL1 Drives Tolerance to Osimertinib in EGFR Mutant Lung Cancer in Permissive Cellular Contexts
source_ledger.finding: ASCL1-dependent tolerance is context-dependent in cell and patient-derived models. Generic plasticity or universal ASCL1 dependence would rebrand or overstate prior results.

source_ledger.title: Focal adhesion kinase-YAP signaling axis drives drug-tolerant persister cells and residual disease in lung cancer
source_ledger.finding: FAK-YAP promotion of persistence has direct model-based prior evidence. It is not a new mechanism inferred from the 17-gene score.

hypotheses.title: Finite sampling explains part of the kit-dependent mean-score reversal
hypotheses.status: Executed in separate depth-simulation results; causal attribution remains unresolved.
hypotheses.novelty: Established mechanism; potentially new dataset-specific quantitative application
hypotheses.mechanism: With fixed true transcript fractions, depth changes detection and the expectation of the concave log1p score.
predictions: Technical-null log scores change across the observed depth distribution although the expected 17-gene UMI fraction is constant.
Repeated depth thinning attenuates a depth-driven difference; large residual differences in count fractions reject depth-only sufficiency.
falsifiers: Observed differences exceed the depth-only null over reasonable abundance and heterogeneity models.
Differences persist across overlapping-depth patients and nonlog count fractions.
controls: Freeze threshold grid, score, exclusions and patient weights before testing.
Inject a known program shift to quantify power lost by thinning.
Bootstrap patients; thinning replicates are technical replicates.
limits: No proof that real data satisfy multinomial assumptions.
Capture-efficiency changes, composition, ambient RNA and stage/site confounding remain.
Total UMI can itself contain biological variation; standardizing it changes the estimand.

hypotheses.title: Ambient alveolar RNA interacts with low endogenous nuclear RNA
hypotheses.status: Proposed only; ambient-mixture simulation not executed.
hypotheses.novelty: Known mixture mechanism; potentially useful cohort-specific falsification
hypotheses.mechanism: Fixed or varying ambient molecules can have a larger fraction in nuclei with fewer endogenous molecules; uniform thinning alone does not recreate that fraction change.
predictions: Surfactant-marker contributions covary with per-library ambient estimates and appear in justified negative cell types.
A mixture-only simulation predicts the relevant direction and magnitude; corrected/raw comparisons reduce the surfactant component while independent lineage anchors behave differently.
falsifiers: No relevant signal in validated negatives or empty-droplet profiles.
Plausible ambient fractions cannot reproduce the observed contrast.
Differences survive correction and orthogonal same-cell localization with coherent lineage anchors.
controls: Use SFTPC/SFTPB/SFTPD-specific justified negatives, not the whole 17-gene set as a negative signature.
Reject doublets/misannotation and separate library-level background from tumor biology.
Show both constant-contamination-fraction and fixed-ambient-molecule scenarios.
limits: A filtered matrix alone cannot identify the true ambient profile.
SoupX correction is model-dependent and does not prove truth.
Immune cells are imperfect negatives; broad genes including LAMP1 are not alveolar-specific.

hypotheses.title: The same mean score can conceal different within-cell lineage coherence
hypotheses.status: Executed in separately frozen coexpression diagnostic; joint dependence is not causal program validation.
hypotheses.novelty: Established decomposition/permutation concepts; potentially underexplored exact17-gene transfer audit
hypotheses.mechanism: An additive mean score ignores cross-gene dependence. Equal total signature abundance can also produce different log scores when distributed differently across genes.
predictions: Within patient and narrow depth strata, cross-gene permutations preserve per-gene marginals and aggregate mean score but remove coordinated expression.
Observed multi-anchor co-detection or residual covariance exceeds a calibrated sampling null if a coherent lineage program is present.
Means, fraction of coherent cells and surfactant contribution can disagree.
falsifiers: Joint marker behavior is reproduced by depth/ambient/marginal-matched nulls.
Apparent coherence disappears after doublet controls or is equally present in inappropriate negative cells.
controls: Freeze biologically justified groups independently of current group differences.
Do not permute unconditioned across patients or depths.
Use an 18-category multinomial model for 17 genes plus other to preserve count competition; stratified marginal permutations alone need not produce valid total-count vectors.
Include injected coordinated-state positive controls and unrelated abundance-matched marker sets.
limits: Gene covariance cannot alter expected additive mean score when gene marginals are held fixed.
Coexpression is not causal dependency, and failure to detect it in sparse nuclei is not evidence of absence.
No threshold selected on current outcomes can be called validated.

recommended_claim: We tested the sensitivity of a published alveolar signature to finite UMI sampling and within-cell gene coherence in a recently expanded, unmatched lung-cancer cohort; ambient-mixture explanations remain to be tested.
prohibited_claims: New cure or clinical target identified
Rank-based scores eliminate all depth effects
Covariance alone explains a mean additive-score reversal
Correction or downsampling identifies the causal treatment effect
mathematical_constraints: For fixed per-gene marginal distributions, covariance cannot alter the expected additive mean-log score.
A signature UMI fraction is conditionally mean-unbiased under fixed-composition multinomial sampling; real assays need not obey that null.
Count-fraction and mean-log comparisons are different estimands; disagreement alone does not identify which is biologically true.
